source.title: Singularity-aware Optimization via Randomized Geometric Probing: Towards Stable Non-smooth Optimization
source.authors: Ruoran Xu; Borong She; Xiao-Bo Jin; Qiu-Feng Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out accuracy for multiple optimizers across batch sizes, giving a different-method test of whether batch size changes the generalization outcome.
record.gate_note: The paper reports best test accuracy across epochs. Results comparing S-Adam with AdamW and Prox-SGD are included where they bear on the batch-size claim. Its own generalization-gap and optimizer-stability arguments are not measurements of training-versus-test gap.
record.test_reason: Experiment 2 measures held-out accuracy across batch sizes 2, 4, 16 and 64 for pretrained ResNet18 models. Table 7 establishes a fixed 20-epoch budget. This bears on V5 in a small-batch fine-tuning setting, although the study does not establish that its batch sizes exceed a workload-dependent large-batch threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but 'consistently outperforms' needs qualification: S-Adam loses to Prox-SGD on Imagewoof2-160 at batch 64 (84.60% versus 86.71%). The authors conclude that geometric damping stabilizes non-smooth optimization and improves best test accuracy particularly in QAT and extreme small-batch settings, with its advantage generally narrowing as batches grow.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes S-Adam with randomized geometric probing and adaptive damping; it does not reproduce the original large-batch comparison recipes or directly measure the train-test generalization gap.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies by optimizer, dataset, batch size, probe count, damping intensity, perturbation scale, and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: S-Adam generally improves best test accuracy over AdamW and Prox-SGD in QAT and small-batch experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometry-dependent damping can improve optimizer performance in these non-smooth training settings; superiority of the proposed adaptive optimizer does not itself test V4.

fits_no_version.finding: LGI estimates local geometric instability; Appendix F develops a conditional stability-bound argument for damping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric damping may improve algorithmic stability. Neither the LGI calculation nor this bound measures V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap ranking.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper reports best test accuracy across epochs but not training accuracy or train-test gaps. The batch-size comparisons report results for batch sizes 4, 16, and 64, but do not establish a general large-batch penalty under fixed epoch budgets. The paper's abstract also mentions high-noise small-batch experiments; Table 3 reports batch size 2.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's QAT optimizer comparisons and Table 2's hyperparameter ablations are omitted because they do not test a claim version's named condition as directly as the batch-size comparisons. Table 3's batch-size-2 accuracy comparisons are included (R1–R12).

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus standard SGD or momentum SGD under the specified tuning conditions. Prox-SGD uses an L1 proximal intervention, and the optimizer recipes differ in regularization.
A demonstrated regime beyond the workload-dependent large-batch threshold; language models; longer training; learning-rate scaling with warmup; normalization or regularization adaptations.
Dropout interventions and removal of dropout together with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, measured generalization gaps, and rankings against norm or margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted accuracy values match the supplied tables. Throughout, the model is pretrained ResNet18 and the named subjects are optimizers. Section 6.3 defines every reported accuracy as the best test accuracy across epochs, including Table 4; Table 7 fixes Experiment 2 at 20 epochs. Missing training accuracy does not prevent a V5 comparison, which concerns held-out performance. Reversed row states describe the direction within the tested batch range, not a challenge to V5's threshold-qualified claim. No significance estimates or repeated-seed uncertainty are supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers against SGD or momentum SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
No comparison with smaller batches for language models; no training-longer or normalization/regularization adaptation study.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or measured generalization-gap ranking.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

relationships.condition: Pretrained ResNet18, Prox-SGD and AdamW, all three datasets, batches 2–64, fixed 20 epochs
relationships.reason: R1–R2, R5–R6, R9–R10 and R13–R30 show monotonically improving best test accuracy with larger batches; this qualifies any extension of the penalty to this small-batch range, without establishing behavior beyond the large-batch threshold.
relationships.display_finding: Monotonically improving best test accuracy with larger batches was reported across the three datasets, but these comparisons remain unverified and establish no harmful batch threshold.

relationships.condition: Pretrained ResNet18, S-Adam, CIFAR10 and Imagewoof2-160, batches 4–64, fixed 20 epochs
relationships.reason: R34–R39 show accuracy increasing throughout the tested range: 90.68% to 94.18% and 81.22% to 84.60%; the range is not demonstrated to exceed a large-batch threshold.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing accuracy throughout the batch range was reported on both datasets, but these comparisons remain unverified and establish no harmful batch threshold.

relationships.condition: Pretrained ResNet18, S-Adam, CIFAR100, batches 4–64, fixed 20 epochs
relationships.reason: R31–R33 show improvement from 66.57% to 74.43%, followed by only a 0.25-point decrease at batch 64; the slight decline has no reported uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: An initial accuracy improvement followed by a small decline was reported, but the comparison remains unverified and the decline lacks uncertainty estimates.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR100, CIFAR10, and Imagewoof2-160; batch sizes 4, 16, and 64
reader_labels.reason: Reported test accuracy often rises with batch size for the compared optimizers, including AdamW and Prox-SGD; the expected large-batch penalty is not evident in these results (R13–R30, R31–R39). This is a test-accuracy comparison, not a direct train-test-gap measure.
